audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Samuel chapter 18, first-pass restored draft
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Jonathan-David covenant, royal clothing and weapons, women's song, Saul's jealousy, harmful-spirit language, spear attacks, military reassignment, Merab and Michal as royal marriage strategy, poverty/status, genital-trophy bride-price, and source tensions.

verses.restored: When David finished speaking to Saul, life of Jonathan was bound to life of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own life.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when he had made an end of speaking unto Saul, that the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.

modern.text: After David had finished speaking with Saul, the souls of Jonathan and David were knit together, and Jonathan loved him as himself.

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י כְּכַלֹּתוֹ֙ לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֶל שָׁא֔וּל וְנֶ֨פֶשׁ֙ יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן נִקְשְׁרָ֖ה בְּנֶ֣פֶשׁ דָּוִ֑ד ויאהבו יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן כְּנַפְשֽׁוֹ

verses.restored: Saul took him that day and did not permit him to return to house of his father.

familiar.text: And Saul took him that day, and would let him go no more home to his father’s house.

modern.text: And from that day Saul kept David with him and did not let him return to his father’s house.

original.text: וַיִּקָּחֵ֥הוּ שָׁא֖וּל בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וְלֹ֣א נְתָנ֔וֹ לָשׁ֖וּב בֵּ֥ית אָבִֽיו

verses.restored: Jonathan cut a covenant with David because he loved him as his own life.

familiar.text: Then Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul.

modern.text: Then Jonathan made a covenant with David because he loved him as himself.

original.text: וַיִּכְרֹ֧ת יְהוֹנָתָ֛ן וְדָוִ֖ד בְּרִ֑ית בְּאַהֲבָת֥וֹ אֹת֖וֹ כְּנַפְשֽׁוֹ

verses.restored: Jonathan stripped robe that was upon him and gave it to David, with his garments, even his sword, bow, and belt.

familiar.text: And Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that was upon him, and gave it to David, and his garments, even to his sword, and to his bow, and to his girdle.

modern.text: And Jonathan removed the robe he was wearing and gave it to David, along with his tunic, his sword, his bow, and his belt. Saul Envies David

original.text: וַיִּתְפַּשֵּׁ֣ט יְהוֹנָתָ֗ן אֶֽת הַמְּעִיל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָלָ֔יו וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֖הוּ לְדָוִ֑ד וּמַדָּ֕יו וְעַד חַרְבּ֥וֹ וְעַד קַשְׁתּ֖וֹ וְעַד חֲגֹרֽוֹ

verses.restored: David went out wherever Saul sent him and acted skillfully. Saul set him over men of war, and it was good in eyes of all people and servants of Saul.

familiar.text: And David went out whithersoever Saul sent him, and behaved himself wisely: and Saul set him over the men of war, and he was accepted in the sight of all the people, and also in the sight of Saul’s servants.

modern.text: So David marched out and prospered in everything Saul sent him to do, and Saul set him over the men of war. And this was pleasing in the sight of all the people, and of Saul’s officers as well.

original.text: וַיֵּצֵ֨א דָוִ֜ד בְּכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׁלָחֶ֤נּוּ שָׁאוּל֙ יַשְׂכִּ֔יל וַיְשִׂמֵ֣הוּ שָׁא֔וּל עַ֖ל אַנְשֵׁ֣י הַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וַיִּיטַב֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י כָל הָעָ֔ם וְגַ֕ם בְּעֵינֵ֖י עַבְדֵ֥י שָׁאֽוּל

verses.restored: When they came, as David returned from striking Philistine, women came out from all cities of Israel, singing and dancing to meet Saul the king, with tambourines, rejoicing, and three-stringed instruments.

familiar.text: And it came to pass as they came, when David was returned from the slaughter of the Philistine, that the women came out of all cities of Israel, singing and dancing, to meet king Saul, with tabrets, with joy, and with instruments of musick.

modern.text: As the troops were returning home after David had killed the Philistine, the women came out of all the cities of Israel to meet King Saul with singing and dancing, with joyful songs, and with tambourines and other instruments.

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י בְּבוֹאָ֗ם בְּשׁ֤וּב דָּוִד֙ מֵהַכּ֣וֹת אֶת הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔י וַתֵּצֶ֨אנָה הַנָּשִׁ֜ים מִכָּל עָרֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לשור וְהַמְּחֹל֔וֹת לִקְרַ֖את שָׁא֣וּל הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ בְּתֻפִּ֥ים בְּשִׂמְחָ֖ה וּבְשָׁלִשִֽׁים

verses.restored: Women who played answered one another and said, Saul has struck his thousands, and David his ten-thousands.

familiar.text: And the women answered one another as they played, and said, Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands.

modern.text: And as the women danced, they sang out: “Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands.”

original.text: וַֽתַּעֲנֶ֛ינָה הַנָּשִׁ֥ים הַֽמְשַׂחֲק֖וֹת וַתֹּאמַ֑רְןָ הִכָּ֤ה שָׁאוּל֙ באלפו וְדָוִ֖ד בְּרִבְבֹתָֽיו

verses.restored: Saul became very angry, and this word was evil in his eyes. He said, They have given David ten-thousands, but to me they have given thousands. What more can he have but kingdom?

familiar.text: And Saul was very wroth, and the saying displeased him; and he said, They have ascribed unto David ten thousands, and to me they have ascribed but thousands: and what can he have more but the kingdom?

modern.text: And Saul was furious and resented this song. “They have ascribed tens of thousands to David,” he said, “but only thousands to me. What more can he have but the kingdom?”

original.text: וַיִּ֨חַר לְשָׁא֜וּל מְאֹ֗ד וַיֵּ֤רַע בְּעֵינָיו֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר נָתְנ֤וּ לְדָוִד֙ רְבָב֔וֹת וְלִ֥י נָתְנ֖וּ הָאֲלָפִ֑ים וְע֥וֹד ל֖וֹ אַ֥ךְ הַמְּלוּכָֽה

verses.restored: Saul watched David with suspicion from that day onward.

familiar.text: And Saul eyed David from that day and forward.

modern.text: And from that day forward Saul kept a jealous eye on David.

original.text: וַיְהִ֥י שָׁא֖וּל עון אֶת דָּוִ֑ד מֵהַיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא וָהָֽלְאָה

verses.restored: On next day a harmful spirit from Divine rushed upon Saul, and he raved/prophesied within house while David played with his hand as day by day. Spear was in Saul's hand.

familiar.text: And it came to pass on the morrow, that the evil spirit from God came upon Saul, and he prophesied in the midst of the house: and David played with his hand, as at other times: and there was a javelin in Saul’s hand.

modern.text: The next day a spirit of distress sent from God came upon Saul, and he prophesied inside the house while David played the harp as usual. Now Saul was holding a spear,

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י מִֽמָּחֳרָ֗ת וַתִּצְלַ֣ח רוּחַ֩ אֱלֹהִ֨ים רָעָ֤ה אֶל שָׁאוּל֙ וַיִּתְנַבֵּ֣א בְתוֹךְ הַבַּ֔יִת וְדָוִ֛ד מְנַגֵּ֥ן בְּיָד֖וֹ כְּי֣וֹם בְּי֑וֹם וְהַחֲנִ֖ית בְּיַד שָׁאֽוּל

verses.restored: Saul hurled spear and said, I will strike David into wall. David turned aside from before him twice.

familiar.text: And Saul cast the javelin; for he said, I will smite David even to the wall with it. And David avoided out of his presence twice.

modern.text: and he hurled it, thinking, “I will pin David to the wall.” But David eluded him twice.

original.text: וַיָּ֤טֶל שָׁאוּל֙ אֶֽת הַחֲנִ֔ית וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אַכֶּ֥ה בְדָוִ֖ד וּבַקִּ֑יר וַיִּסֹּ֥ב דָּוִ֛ד מִפָּנָ֖יו פַּעֲמָֽיִם

verses.restored: Saul was afraid before David because YHWH was with him and had turned aside from Saul.

familiar.text: And Saul was afraid of David, because the LORD was with him, and was departed from Saul.

modern.text: So Saul was afraid of David, because the LORD was with David but had departed from Saul.

original.text: וַיִּרָ֥א שָׁא֖וּל מִלִּפְנֵ֣י דָוִ֑ד כִּֽי הָיָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וּמֵעִ֥ם שָׁא֖וּל סָֽר

verses.restored: Saul removed him from with him and set him as commander of thousand, and David went out and came in before people.

familiar.text: Therefore Saul removed him from him, and made him his captain over a thousand; and he went out and came in before the people.

modern.text: Therefore Saul sent David away and gave him command of a thousand men. David led the troops out to battle and back,

original.text: וַיְסִרֵ֤הוּ שָׁאוּל֙ מֵֽעִמּ֔וֹ וַיְשִׂמֵ֥הוּ ל֖וֹ שַׂר אָ֑לֶף וַיֵּצֵ֥א וַיָּבֹ֖א לִפְנֵ֥י הָעָֽם

verses.restored: David acted skillfully in all his ways, and YHWH was with him.

familiar.text: And David behaved himself wisely in all his ways; and the LORD was with him.

modern.text: and he continued to prosper in all his ways, because the LORD was with him.

original.text: וַיְהִ֥י דָוִ֛ד לְכָל דָּרְכָ֖ו מַשְׂכִּ֑יל וַֽיהוָ֖ה עִמּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Saul saw that he acted very skillfully and dreaded him.

familiar.text: Wherefore when Saul saw that he behaved himself very wisely, he was afraid of him.

modern.text: When Saul saw that David was very successful, he was afraid of him.

original.text: וַיַּ֣רְא שָׁא֔וּל אֲשֶׁר ה֖וּא מַשְׂכִּ֣יל מְאֹ֑ד וַיָּ֖גָר מִפָּנָֽיו

verses.restored: All Israel and Judah loved David, because he went out and came in before them.

familiar.text: But all Israel and Judah loved David, because he went out and came in before them.

modern.text: But all Israel and Judah loved David, because he was leading them out to battle and back. David Marries Michal

original.text: וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וִיהוּדָ֔ה אֹהֵ֖ב אֶת דָּוִ֑ד כִּֽי ה֛וּא יוֹצֵ֥א וָבָ֖א לִפְנֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: Saul said to David, Here is my older daughter Merab. I will give her to you as wife. Only be for me a son of valor and fight battles of YHWH. Saul said, Let not my hand be against him, but let hand of Philistines be against him.

familiar.text: And Saul said to David, Behold my elder daughter Merab, her will I give thee to wife: only be thou valiant for me, and fight the LORD’s battles. For Saul said, Let not mine hand be upon him, but let the hand of the Philistines be upon him.

modern.text: Then Saul said to David, “Here is my older daughter Merab. I will give her to you in marriage. Only be valiant for me and fight the LORD’s battles.” But Saul was thinking, “I need not raise my hand against him; let the hand of the Philistines be against him.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֜וּל אֶל דָּוִ֗ד הִנֵּה֩ בִתִּ֨י הַגְּדוֹלָ֤ה מֵרַב֙ אֹתָהּ֙ אֶתֶּן לְךָ֣ לְאִשָּׁ֔ה אַ֚ךְ הֱיֵה לִּ֣י לְבֶן חַ֔יִל וְהִלָּחֵ֖ם מִלְחֲמ֣וֹת יְהוָ֑ה וְשָׁא֣וּל אָמַ֗ר אַל תְּהִ֤י יָדִי֙ בּ֔וֹ וּתְהִי ב֖וֹ יַד פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים

verses.restored: David said to Saul, Who am I, and what is my life or clan of my father in Israel, that I should become son-in-law to king?

familiar.text: And David said unto Saul, Who am I? and what is my life, or my father’s family in Israel, that I should be son in law to the king?

modern.text: And David said to Saul, “Who am I, and what is my family or my father’s clan in Israel, that I should become the son-in-law of the king?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד אֶל שָׁא֗וּל מִ֤י אָֽנֹכִי֙ וּמִ֣י חַיַּ֔י מִשְׁפַּ֥חַת אָבִ֖י בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּֽי אֶהְיֶ֥ה חָתָ֖ן לַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: At time Merab daughter of Saul was to be given to David, she was given to Adriel the Meholathite as wife.

familiar.text: But it came to pass at the time when Merab Saul’s daughter should have been given to David, that she was given unto Adriel the Meholathite to wife.

modern.text: So when it was time to give Saul’s daughter Merab to David, she was given in marriage to Adriel of Meholah.

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י בְּעֵ֥ת תֵּ֛ת אֶת מֵרַ֥ב בַּת שָׁא֖וּל לְדָוִ֑ד וְהִ֧יא נִתְּנָ֛ה לְעַדְרִיאֵ֥ל הַמְּחֹלָתִ֖י לְאִשָּֽׁה

verses.restored: Michal daughter of Saul loved David. They told Saul, and matter was right in his eyes.

familiar.text: And Michal Saul’s daughter loved David: and they told Saul, and the thing pleased him.

modern.text: Now Saul’s daughter Michal loved David, and when this was reported to Saul, it pleased him.

original.text: וַתֶּאֱהַ֛ב מִיכַ֥ל בַּת שָׁא֖וּל אֶת דָּוִ֑ד וַיַּגִּ֣דוּ לְשָׁא֔וּל וַיִּשַׁ֥ר הַדָּבָ֖ר בְּעֵינָֽיו

verses.restored: Saul said, I will give her to him, and she shall become a snare to him, and hand of Philistines shall be against him. Saul said to David a second time, You shall become my son-in-law today.

familiar.text: And Saul said, I will give him her, that she may be a snare to him, and that the hand of the Philistines may be against him. Wherefore Saul said to David, Thou shalt this day be my son in law in the one of the twain.

modern.text: “I will give her to David,” Saul thought, “so that she may be a snare to him, and the hand of the Philistines may be against him.” So Saul said to David, “For a second time now you can be my son-in-law.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֜וּל אֶתְּנֶ֤נָּה לּוֹ֙ וּתְהִי ל֣וֹ לְמוֹקֵ֔שׁ וּתְהִי ב֖וֹ יַד פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שָׁאוּל֙ אֶל דָּוִ֔ד בִּשְׁתַּ֛יִם תִּתְחַתֵּ֥ן בִּ֖י הַיּֽוֹם

verses.restored: Saul commanded his servants, Speak to David in secret, saying, Look, king delights in you, and all his servants love you. Now become son-in-law to king.

familiar.text: And Saul commanded his servants, saying, Commune with David secretly, and say, Behold, the king hath delight in thee, and all his servants love thee: now therefore be the king’s son in law.

modern.text: Then Saul ordered his servants, “Speak to David privately and tell him, ‘Behold, the king is pleased with you, and all his servants love you. Now therefore, become his son-in-law.’”

original.text: וַיְצַ֨ו שָׁא֜וּל אֶת עֲבָדָ֗ו דַּבְּר֨וּ אֶל דָּוִ֤ד בַּלָּט֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִנֵּ֨ה חָפֵ֤ץ בְּךָ֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְכָל עֲבָדָ֖יו אֲהֵב֑וּךָ וְעַתָּ֖ה הִתְחַתֵּ֥ן בַּמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Servants of Saul spoke these words in ears of David. David said, Is it light in your eyes to become son-in-law to king, when I am a poor and lightly esteemed man?

familiar.text: And Saul’s servants spake those words in the ears of David. And David said, Seemeth it to you a light thing to be a king’s son in law, seeing that I am a poor man, and lightly esteemed?

modern.text: But when Saul’s servants relayed these words to David, he replied, “Does it seem trivial in your sight to be the son-in-law of the king? I am a poor man and lightly esteemed.”

original.text: וַֽיְדַבְּר֞וּ עַבְדֵ֤י שָׁאוּל֙ בְּאָזְנֵ֣י דָוִ֔ד אֶת הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗ד הַֽנְקַלָּ֤ה בְעֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ הִתְחַתֵּ֣ן בַּמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְאָנֹכִ֖י אִֽישׁ רָ֥שׁ וְנִקְלֶֽה

verses.restored: Servants of Saul reported to him, saying, According to these words David spoke.

familiar.text: And the servants of Saul told him, saying, On this manner spake David.

modern.text: And the servants told Saul what David had said.

original.text: וַיַּגִּ֜דוּ עַבְדֵ֥י שָׁא֛וּל ל֖וֹ לֵאמֹ֑ר כַּדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה דִּבֶּ֥ר דָּוִֽד

verses.restored: Saul said, Thus say to David: King does not desire bride-price except one hundred foreskins of Philistines, to take vengeance on enemies of king. Saul planned to make David fall by hand of Philistines.

familiar.text: And Saul said, Thus shall ye say to David, The king desireth not any dowry, but an hundred foreskins of the Philistines, to be avenged of the king’s enemies. But Saul thought to make David fall by the hand of the Philistines.

modern.text: Saul replied, “Say to David, ‘The king desires no other dowry but a hundred Philistine foreskins as revenge on his enemies.’” But Saul intended to cause David’s death at the hands of the Philistines.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֜וּל כֹּֽה תֹאמְר֣וּ לְדָוִ֗ד אֵֽין חֵ֤פֶץ לַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ בְּמֹ֔הַר כִּ֗י בְּמֵאָה֙ עָרְל֣וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים לְהִנָּקֵ֖ם בְּאֹיְבֵ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְשָׁא֣וּל חָשַׁ֔ב לְהַפִּ֥יל אֶת דָּוִ֖ד בְּיַד פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים

verses.restored: His servants told David these words, and matter was right in David's eyes to become son-in-law to king. Days had not been fulfilled.

familiar.text: And when his servants told David these words, it pleased David well to be the king’s son in law: and the days were not expired.

modern.text: When the servants reported these terms to David, he was pleased to become the king’s son-in-law. Before the wedding day arrived,

original.text: וַיַּגִּ֨דוּ עֲבָדָ֤יו לְדָוִד֙ אֶת הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה וַיִּשַׁ֤ר הַדָּבָר֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י דָוִ֔ד לְהִתְחַתֵּ֖ן בַּמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְלֹ֥א מָלְא֖וּ הַיָּמִֽים

verses.restored: David arose and went, he and his men, and struck two hundred men among Philistines. David brought their foreskins, and they counted them out fully to king so he might become son-in-law to king. Saul gave him Michal his daughter as wife.

familiar.text: Wherefore David arose and went, he and his men, and slew of the Philistines two hundred men; and David brought their foreskins, and they gave them in full tale to the king, that he might be the king’s son in law. And Saul gave him Michal his daughter to wife.

modern.text: David and his men went out and killed two hundred Philistines. He brought their foreskins and presented them as payment in full to become the king’s son-in-law. Then Saul gave his daughter Michal to David in marriage.

original.text: וַיָּ֨קָם דָּוִ֜ד וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ ה֣וּא וַאֲנָשָׁ֗יו וַיַּ֣ךְ בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּים֮ מָאתַ֣יִם אִישׁ֒ וַיָּבֵ֤א דָוִד֙ אֶת עָרְלֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם וַיְמַלְא֣וּם לַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לְהִתְחַתֵּ֖ן בַּמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיִּתֶּן ל֥וֹ שָׁא֛וּל אֶת מִיכַ֥ל בִּתּ֖וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה

verses.restored: Saul saw and knew that YHWH was with David, and Michal daughter of Saul loved him.

familiar.text: And Saul saw and knew that the LORD was with David, and that Michal Saul’s daughter loved him.

modern.text: When Saul realized that the LORD was with David and that his daughter Michal loved David,

verses.restored: Saul was still more afraid before David, and Saul became enemy of David all days.

familiar.text: And Saul was yet the more afraid of David; and Saul became David’s enemy continually.

modern.text: he grew even more afraid of David. So from then on Saul was David’s enemy.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אסֶף שָׁא֗וּל לֵרֹ֛א מִפְּנֵ֥י דָוִ֖ד ע֑וֹד וַיְהִ֥י שָׁא֛וּל אֹיֵ֥ב אֶת דָּוִ֖ד כָּל הַיָּמִֽים

verses.restored: Princes of Philistines went out, and whenever they went out David acted more skillfully than all servants of Saul, and his name became greatly esteemed.

familiar.text: Then the princes of the Philistines went forth: and it came to pass, after they went forth, that David behaved himself more wisely than all the servants of Saul; so that his name was much set by.

modern.text: Every time the Philistine commanders came out for battle, David was more successful than all of Saul’s officers, so that his name was highly esteemed.

original.text: וַיֵּצְא֖וּ שָׂרֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיְהִ֣י מִדֵּ֣י צֵאתָ֗ם שָׂכַ֤ל דָּוִד֙ מִכֹּל֙ עַבְדֵ֣י שָׁא֔וּל וַיִּיקַ֥ר שְׁמ֖וֹ מְאֹֽד

translation_notes: Jonathan's love and covenant are intense political and personal bonds. The text does not require erasing queer readings, nor does it permit forcing a single modern category onto ancient relationships.
Jonathan's transfer of robe and weapons may signal affection, covenant, rank, or political recognition. It is not proof that hereditary power is privately transferable without public accountability.
Saul's confinement of David to court and repeated military appointments place a young subordinate under royal control.
The women's victory song is communal performance, not the cause of Saul's violence. Women are not responsible for male jealousy, rivalry, or abuse.
The harmful-spirit and raving/prophesying language must not stigmatize mental illness, trauma, neurodivergence, or altered states. Saul remains responsible for two spear attacks.
David's avoidance of the spear is survival under domestic and workplace violence; victims are not obligated to remain available to an abuser.
Saul offers Merab and Michal as instruments of strategy. Neither daughter is property, and the text gives no basis for assuming either woman's consent to the arrangements.
Michal's love is named, but love does not erase the royal power imbalance, the lethal bride-price, or her father's manipulation.
The foreskin bride-price is mutilation, trophy violence, and ethnicized killing. It cannot be romanticized as courtship, masculinity, covenant proof, or a sexual joke.
'Battles of YHWH' is Saul's manipulative framing of a plot to have David killed and cannot sanctify political warfare.
David's success and popular esteem do not establish moral perfection or immunity from later accountability.
safety_note: Maximum safeguards: Do not blame women for Saul's jealousy, romanticize spear attacks, diagnose distress as demonic, treat Jonathan and David as usable ammunition against queer or non-queer people, or present royal marriage arrangements as consent. Merab and Michal are not rewards or traps by nature; Saul makes them instruments. The genital-trophy bride-price is lethal mutilation and must never be celebrated, imitated, eroticized, or preached as heroic masculinity.
